import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# matrix_ops.m
# Linear algebra and the indexing conventions that trip up MATLAB->Python ports
# (1-based indexing, column-major order, "end", elementwise vs matrix product).
# Written from scratch for the matlab-to-python-agent demo (public, no client data).

A = np.array([[4, -2, 1], [-2, 4, -2], [1, -2, 4]], dtype=float)     # symmetric positive definite
b = np.array([[11], [-16], [17]], dtype=float)

x        = np.linalg.solve(A, b);                  # MATLAB: mldivide -> np.linalg.solve
detA     = np.linalg.det(A);                       # MATLAB: det -> np.linalg.det
Ainv     = np.linalg.inv(A);                       # MATLAB: inv -> np.linalg.inv
ev       = np.sort(np.linalg.eig(A)[0]);           # MATLAB: sort, eig -> np.sort, np.linalg.eig
residual = np.linalg.norm(A @ x - b);              # MATLAB: norm -> np.linalg.norm

B      = np.reshape(np.arange(1, 13), (3, 4), order='F');      # MATLAB: reshape -> np.reshape
B_flat = np.reshape(B, (-1,), order='F'); # MATLAB: (:) -> np.reshape with order='F'
B_flat = B_flat[np.newaxis, :]            # MATLAB: ' -> transpose (1x12 row vector)
sub    = B[1:3, [0, -1]];          # rows 2-3 (0-indexed 1:3), first and last column ([0, -1])
K      = np.kron(np.eye(2), np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]]));     # MATLAB: kron, eye -> np.kron, np.eye

C  = A * A.T + 2;                  # elementwise product
D  = A @ A.T;                      # matrix product
tr = np.trace(D);                  # MATLAB: trace -> np.trace
cs = np.cumsum(B, axis=1);         # MATLAB: cumsum -> np.cumsum
mask_sum = np.sum(B[B > 6]);       # MATLAB: sum -> np.sum
row_max  = np.max(B, axis=1, keepdims=True).T;  # MATLAB: max -> np.max
